consequence.statement: Hubble TLS certificates will have a shorter validity duration (365 days instead of 1095 days), preventing validation failures on recent macOS versions that reject certificates with expirations longer than 825 days.

original.statement: The default value of Helm value hubble.tls.auto.certValidityDuration has been lowered from 1095 days to 365 days to prevent certificate validation failures on recent versions of macOS.

decision.reason: [ev-0debb0d83ac2] says only that the default of `hubble.tls.auto.certValidityDuration` was lowered from 1095 to 365 days, because recent macOS versions reject certificates that expire after more than 825 days. The validators confirm this default change against the values files [ev-28e0ccb5774a] [ev-39a22d88e2f5]. Nothing in the evidence says anything fails, is rejected or stops being honoured: auto-generated certificates just get a shorter validity. So behavior-change (a review item) is the right kind, and the proposed statement matches the evidence.
